temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Small sprouts, halved 375°F / 190°C · 12 min 400°F / 205°C · 16 min Medium sprouts, about 1 inch, halved 375°F / 190°C · 15 min 400°F / 205°C · 20 min Large sprouts, quartered 375°F / 190°C · 18 min 400°F / 205°C · 24 min Raw cores and burnt leaves A Brussels sprout is a tight bundle of leaves wrapped around a dense, solid core. The loose outer leaves dry and crisp almost at once in an air fryer, but heat has to work its way through layer after layer to reach the middle, so a whole sprout can be scorched outside and still hard and sulphurous at the heart. Halving them is the main fix, because it exposes the core and halves the distance the heat has to travel. Then the cut face matters. Laid flat against the hot basket, that face caramelises into a sweet, nutty crust, while the domed side gets crisp leaves from the moving air. Turn them cut side down for the first stretch, and only then start shaking. Large sprouts should be quartered, or the centre still lags. Worked example A pound of medium sprouts, trimmed and halved, tossed with a tablespoon and a half of oil and salt. Preheat 4 minutes, set them cut side down and cook at 375°F for 15 minutes, shaking twice in the second half. Small halved sprouts need about 12 minutes and quartered large ones about 18. In a conventional oven the same tray takes 400°F for about 20 minutes. How to tell they are done Push a knife into the thickest part of the core: it should go in easily, like a cooked potato. The cut face should be deep golden to dark brown, and some outer leaves will have come loose and turned crisp and almost black; those are the best part. A grey colour or a strong cabbage smell means they cooked too long at too low a heat, or were steamed in a crowded basket. Before they go in Trim the dry stalk end and pull off any yellow leaves. Cut through the stalk so each half holds together. Toss with oil until every cut face is glossy. Balsamic glaze, honey or a squeeze of lemon goes on after cooking, since sugar burns at the end of a hot cook. About 15 minutes at 375°F for halved medium sprouts, shaken twice. Small ones take around 12 minutes and quartered large ones around 18. Should I cut Brussels sprouts in half for the air fryer? Yes. Whole sprouts burn outside before the dense core cooks; halving them exposes the core and gives a flat face that browns. Why are my sprouts still hard in the middle? They were too large for the time. Quarter big sprouts, and check the core with a knife before taking them out. Do I start sprouts cut side up or down? Down. The flat face caramelises against the hot basket, then the shakes crisp the leaves. What is the oven equivalent for Brussels sprouts? 400°F for around 20 minutes on a tray in a conventional oven, or 375°F for 17 minutes in a fan oven.
